label: value-rows-need-consumer-or-provenance
name: A pinned expected value needs a consumer, a placeholder fixture value needs a don't-care comment, an opaque digest needs documented provenance
description: What breaks: a test row becomes a contract nobody asked for, or a literal nobody can regenerate. A table row makes 'a float NaN stores as +inf' a tested contract while AGENTS.md treats NaN as corruption (4188336250, check 1 as written); pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f in a fixture with no comment (2948257220, suggestion block '// not correct, but it's a don't-care for this usage below' and 'similarly elsewhere'); a hard-coded SHA256 in a Python test with no stated origin (4020335622 'is this crazy magic digest/sha captured/documented anywhere? Where did it come from?'). Procedure (check 1 widened): also flag round placeholder model parameters in fixtures without a comment, and long opaque expected literals (hashes, frozen tables) without a regeneration source or evidence-register entry.
disposition_reason: Check 1 triggers on a conversion between written and expected bits; the corpus adds placeholder fixture values and opaque literals without provenance.
agent_feasibility: yes: existing check 1 procedure plus long opaque literals without a provenance comment and round placeholder values without a comment.

members.concern: A test table row makes 'a float NaN stores as +inf' (and the truncation/tie rounding rows) a tested contract with no consumer, while the repository rule (AGENTS.md) treats NaN as corruption; drop those rows and keep the bf16 round-trip and partner-zero checks.

detection.trigger: A test hunk adds a runtime REQUIRE whose expected side is a literal or table entry that differs from the bits the same test wrote earlier by a conversion, rounding, tie, or a special value changing class (NaN to inf, denormal to zero).
detection.procedure: list the table rows; for each row whose expected value differs from the input by more than a widening, name the accessor the row stores through (set_v / append_v_row) and grep h/ and src/ (excluding t/) for a reader, documented format or AGENTS.md line that depends on the exact bits; read AGENTS.md's NaN rule; compute what the generic converter (the 'would round to 0x3f81' / 'would stay a NaN' alternative the test comment names) gives for the same input.
detection.question: Name the production reader, format or repository rule that breaks if this exact expected value changes; if none, the row pins incidental behavior.

members.quote: This row makes "a float NaN stores as +inf" a tested contract. AGENTS.md treats NaN as corruption; this pins the path that hides it. The truncation and tie rows likewise pin today's rounding, with no named consumer.
members.note: Anchored at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3575 (96a6220ab6), the row `{0x7f800001u, 0x7f80u}, // NaN with payload only in the low bits -> +inf` in SECTION 'float rows truncate to their upper 16 bits, without NaN correction'. Fact relied on: the shift-by-16 truncation store turns a low-payload NaN into +inf; AGENTS.md's NaN-as-corruption rule. Author reply: NaN->inf row, the two rounding-sensitive rows and the 65504 fp16 row removed in c5d44bd86f, exact rows kept, sections renamed; the NaN behavior itself deferred to a follow-up issue.

members.concern: The test fills hw_attn_params with pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f, a value that is not the real model scalar; Wade proposes (as a suggestion block) a comment saying it is incorrect but irrelevant for this test, and asks the same wherever the pattern repeats.

detection.trigger: A test hunk assigns a model parameter (scalar, head count, gqa ratio) a round placeholder literal (1.0f, 4) that differs from any real model value, with no comment, and the code under test does not read that field on the tested path.
detection.procedure: For each parameter field set in the test fixture, grep the production code under test for reads of the field on the exercised path; if the field is unread (or read only in a branch the test does not reach) and the literal is a placeholder, flag the assignment; count repeats of the same fixture block in the file (grep -n 'pre_attn_scalar' t/FILE).
detection.question: Does the test say which fixture values are placeholders that the exercised path ignores, so a reader does not mistake them for a tested contract?

members.quote:
params.pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f; // not correct, but it's a don't-care for this usage below

and similarly elsewhere this is done
members.note: Author: 'fixed in commit 8a6db7243'. Verified at 429249ead6 t/t_hwattention.cpp:95, :575, :1033, :1178 all read `params.pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f;  // not correct, but a don't-care here` (wording shortened from the suggestion). Check 1 fit is partial: same theme (a literal in a test must say what depends on it), but check 1 triggers on expected-side literals in assertions, not on stimulus/fixture literals.

members.concern: A test asserts a hard-coded SHA256 digest over reference checkpoint arrays; he asks where the value came from, whether its provenance is documented, and whether it belongs in the repository's evidence register docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md (which the AGENTS doc points to).

detection.trigger: A test hunk adds an equality assertion against a long opaque literal (a hash hex string, a digest, a checksum, a frozen float table) with no comment or document naming how it was produced.
detection.procedure: For each opaque literal in added test lines (regex for 32+ hex characters or long numeric tables), grep docs/ and AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md for the literal and for an evidence or provenance register the repository mandates; read the nearest comment above the assertion; check whether the PR body or docs name the generating command, date and source revision. Ask for the registration if the repository has a register.
detection.question: Can a reader regenerate or trace this literal from a documented source, and is it registered where the repository says such frozen evidence must be listed?

members.quote: is this crazy 'magic' digest/sha captured/documented anywhere? Where did it come from? Are these supposed to be listed in the ANCHORED_EVIDENCE doc (I just happened to see that referenced from the AGENTS doc)
members.note: Author: 'Good catch: it was not registered.' The literal is a SHA256 over all D128 checkpoint arrays of the tiny chunked_stress native reference, frozen 2026-09-11 from the v1 NumPy reference, kept as a regression lock across v2/v3. The PR file list now includes docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md (+1 -0) and the body says 'The frozen tiny checkpoint digest is registered in docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md', so the register was updated. Check 1 shares the theme (an expected literal needs a named consumer or documented source) but its trigger (a conversion/rounding difference) would not fire. Wade found the register rule by reading the repo's AGENTS doc, i.e. he reads project policy files before commenting.

codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 4557, 4596, asim 244). Claude checks 1 and 2 already encode this with procedures.
